context_only: ## 2. Prior art and the lessons taken

tasks.title: Add the seven run workflow fields
tasks.acceptance:
model.Workflow gains run_max_units, run_max_wall_clock_seconds, run_max_budget_usd, run_max_unit_budget_usd, run_max_unit_retries, runner and notify_cmd with the documented defaults and ranges.
Each numeric field accepts both range endpoints and rejects one step outside; notify_cmd resolves from .tp/local.json only.
tp config --resolved, tp config --extract and tp validate --project cover all seven (test 16, 69).
tasks.closed_reason:
- model.Workflow now carries §7's seven run fields with the documented defaults — run_max_units 100, run_max_wall_clock_seconds 28800, both budgets 0 (disabled / flag omitted) as decimal dollars, run_max_unit_retries 1, runner "claude" as raw JSON so the resolver (not this layer) tells its three shapes apart, and notify_cmd; the six layerable ones are presence-tracked in WorkflowOverride and resolve through the existing task-override > project-config > built-in path, verified by tests asserting each default and each layer winning per field, including an explicit 0 retries beating a project value.
- Every numeric range is enforced at the same read-time clamp the existing fields use: an out-of-range value is dropped to absent with a warning and resolves to the built-in default. A table test drives each of the five fields through a real .tp/config.json and asserts BOTH endpoints are accepted (1/10000, 60/604800, 0/5, 0/10000, 0/1000) and that one step outside each — one unit for the integers, one cent for the budgets — is rejected, so an inclusive bound cannot pass as exclusive.
- notify_cmd resolves from .tp/local.json only: it is a LocalConfig key, is deliberately absent from knownWorkflowKeys (so a workflow block carrying it reports "unknown workflow key"), and is never hoisted by --extract or compared by --project. Verified by a test where config.json and local.json both name one and the local value wins with the unknown-key warning raised.
- All three config surfaces cover the seven: tp config --resolved reports each with its layer (override/project/default, and local/default for notify_cmd), tp config --extract hoists the six unanimous ones and never notify_cmd, and tp validate --project reports run-field deviations with budgets printed as decimal dollars and runner compared as raw JSON. Dogfooded with the freshly built binary on tp's own repo (all seven report default, runner "claude") and on a scratch project where a per-kind runner map, a local notify_cmd and an out-of-range run_max_units each reported as documented.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... , golangci-lint run, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh all exit 0.

Out of scope: tp set --workflow (and --project) still rejects the five numeric run fields as unknown workflow fields, so they are authorable only by hand-editing .tp/config.json or a task file's workflow block; §5.1's "tp set --workflow run_max_*= above the resolved value" fence assumes that setter exists, so the unattended-fence or run-command task needs it added to editableWorkflowFields/workflowFieldRange with float support for the two budgets.

tasks.title: Resolve the runner field's three shapes
tasks.acceptance:
runner resolves as a template name, a runner object, or a per-kind map with default; an object carrying cmd is a runner and anything else is a map.
A map without default and a runner object without cmd are both usage errors (test 56).
tasks.closed_reason:
- engine.ResolveRunner resolves section 3.2's runner field to the runner one unit kind spawns with, telling the three shapes apart by their JSON alone: a string is a built-in template name, an object carrying cmd is a runner object, and any other object is a per-kind map dispatching each kind to one of the first two with a default key covering the rest, so an object carrying both cmd and default is a runner and one carrying neither is a map; verified by tests over each shape plus the two ambiguous objects, and by mutating the cmd discriminator in both directions (always-false, always-true) and watching exactly the shape tests go red before restoring it.
- Test 56's two named usage errors — a map without default, a runner object without cmd — are both *engine.RunnerShapeError, and internal/cli/root.go maps that type to exit 2 (USAGE) with the error's own three-shapes hint, distinct from the run-lock precedent's exit 4 because no wait or retry can fix a configuration that does not say what to spawn; the dispatcher's classification was extracted from Execute into dispatchError so the mapping is callable, and the new CLI test was watched failing (exit 1, exit-1 default hint) against the unwired code before the branch was added.
- Gate green, each step run separately: go test -race ./... = 0, golangci-lint run = 0, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh = 0.
Out of scope: the map's entries are validated whole on every resolve, so a driver resolving per unit re-validates the same map each time; if that ever shows up as cost, the fix is a resolve-once-at-run-start cache in the driver task, not here.

tasks.title: Ship both built-in runner templates
tasks.acceptance:
The claude template resolves to its documented argv including --permission-mode auto, appending --max-budget-usd only when run_max_unit_budget_usd is non-zero; opencode resolves to run with the prompt.
Every placeholder resolves, and an unresolved one is a usage error raised before any child is spawned (test 10).
tasks.closed_reason:
- engine.BuiltinRunner ships section 3.2.1's two templates: claude resolves to cmd claude with the documented argv -p {prompt} --output-format stream-json --verbose --permission-mode auto and spend_key total_cost_usd, appending --max-budget-usd {max_budget_usd} only when the resolved run_max_unit_budget_usd is non-zero (0 omits the pair rather than passing a literal 0), and opencode resolves to run with the prompt, no budget flag and no spend_key so cap-budget is inert for it; verified in both directions and by mutating the budget condition to always-true and always-false, which reddened the zero-budget assertions and the non-zero assertions respectively and nothing else.
- engine.ExpandArgs resolves all five placeholders ({prompt}, {max_budget_usd}, {unit_id}, {unit_kind}, {log_path}), expands {max_budget_usd} to a literal 0 for a positional template, scans each argument once so a substituted value is never rescanned, leaves braces that are not placeholder-shaped untouched, and reports anything else as a *engine.RunnerTemplateError naming runner.args[N]; internal/cli/root.go maps that error and an unknown template name to exit 2 beside the shape branch.
- engine.ResolveUnitRunner composes section 3.2's shape resolution with the template layer into one pure function returning argv, which is how 'before any child is spawned' is kept structurally: the unresolved-placeholder test points a runner's cmd at a script that would touch a sentinel and asserts the sentinel is absent after the error. Verified by mutating the unresolved-placeholder branch into a no-op that leaves the token literal, which reddened exactly those tests plus the CLI classification test.
- engine.UnitPrompt renders the fixed per-kind instruction {prompt} expands to, built from the kind's own BriefCommand, and returns empty for a kind outside the eight.
- Gate green, each step run separately: go test -race ./... 0, golangci-lint run 0, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh 0.
Out of scope: section 6.3's per-kind ["--agent", "<name>"] append is left to the plugin-agents task; BuiltinRunner takes the whole TemplateValues (which carries Kind) so it needs no new parameter to grow it.

tasks.title: Add the TP_RUNNER_SEAM test seam
tasks.acceptance:
TP_RUNNER_SEAM resolves to a runner whose args are the documented positional list and whose spend_key is total_cost_usd, outranking every layer including CLI.
The fake runner records each invocation's argv, environment, spawn time and exit time (test 1).
tasks.closed_reason:
- engine.SeamRunner resolves TP_RUNNER_SEAM to a runner whose cmd is the variable value, whose args are section 3.2.1 positional list {unit_kind} {unit_id} {log_path} {max_budget_usd} and whose spend_key is total_cost_usd, and ResolveUnitRunner reads it before the runner field so it outranks every layer including a CLI-level value; verified in both arms (without the seam the CLI-level runner object wins, with it the seam wins even over a value the resolver rejects), watched failing first with SeamRunner deliberately unwired, then by mutating the seam into a no-op, which reddened exactly the five seam tests and left the control arm and every other runner test green.
- internal/fakerunner is the fake runner the seam pins: a real executable that claims its sequence number by exclusive file creation and records each invocation argv, whole environment, spawn time and exit time, exits with a scripted code and writes the final total_cost_usd log line, with fakerunner.Records reading the completed records back in order; verified by running it rather than reading it, including two concurrent children whose recorded windows overlap (test 1 and section 10.1 test 5), and by mutating the recorded spawn time, the argv/environment capture and the scripted exit each into a no-op, which reddened exactly the overlap test, the two argv tests and the exit-code test respectively, restored byte-identically each time.
Out of scope: a doc-comment paragraph is duplicated verbatim in internal/engine/configresolve.go (ResolveWorkflowLayers) and in internal/engine/runnertemplate_test.go (TestBuiltinRunner_ClaudeArgv), a copy-paste artifact left by earlier units.

tasks.title: Read spend from the runner log
tasks.acceptance:
After a child exits the driver reads total_cost_usd for claude or the declared spend_key, and reports spend null for a runner declaring none.
A runner with no spend_key leaves cap-budget inert and is reported once at run start; a per-kind map names its unmetered kinds (tests 11, 66).

tasks.title: Define the eight unit kinds
tasks.acceptance:
An eight-kind enum carries each kind's durable-write predicate and concurrency from the table.
Each predicate is decidable from the artifacts it names with no baseline, and the role predicate ignores blank and whitespace-only lines (tests 18, 48, 59).
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/engine/unitkind.go defines UnitKind as §3.3's eight kinds in table order (implement, review-role, review-record, review-resolve, decompose, audit-role, audit-record, audit-fix), each carrying its concurrency (Concurrency()/Concurrent(): only the two role kinds are ConcurrencySiblingRoles, every other kind and any unknown value is alone) and its durable-write predicate (DurableWrite(UnitTarget)); verified by table tests over all eight kinds asserting the enum, the order, the defensive copy, ParseUnitKind's rejection of near-misses, and each kind's concurrency value.
- Every predicate is decidable from the artifacts §3.3 names for it with no baseline: TestUnitKind_DurableWrite_DecidableWithNoBaseline runs each kind in a fresh temp dir where the artifacts are written before the predicate is ever called (so no 'before' observation exists), asserts a repeat call answers identically (state, not delta), and pairs each with a one-artifact-short case plus a nothing-written case; the audit-fix case passes on a row disposed with no code change at all (test 18), and an unknown kind is never complete.
- The role predicate reads content lines only: TestUnitKind_RolePredicate_ContentLinesOnly runs both role kinds over a trailing newline, a file of blank and whitespace-only lines, an empty file, an unparseable line, a truncated row, a non-object line, and a missing file (tests 48, 59), with the .part-only case failing because the rename that completes the write never happened.
- Gate green on the committed tree: go test -race ./... = 0, golangci-lint run = 0, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh = 0.
Out of scope: the recorded round-file name format (review-round-<N>.ndjson / audit-round-<N>.ndjson) is now spelled in three places — internal/cli/review_record.go, internal/cli/audit_record.go and engine.roundFilePath — so the two writers and this reader can drift; centralizing it belongs to whichever later task next touches the record paths.

tasks.title: Map each unit kind to its brief command
tasks.acceptance:
Each kind resolves to the documented brief_command, with the record kinds' merge step skipped when merged.ndjson already exists.
A unit succeeded when it exited 0 and its durable write is present; either alone is a failed attempt (tests 51, 57).
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/engine/briefcommand.go maps every §3.3.1 unit kind to the brief_command the oracle supplies: tp next --brief (implement), tp review/tp audit <spec> (the role kinds), tp review/tp audit <spec> --status (review-resolve / audit-fix), tp resume (decompose), and the two-step record brief '[ -f $TP_ROUND_DIR/merged.ndjson ] || tp <phase> --merge $TP_ROUND_DIR/role-*.ndjson -o $TP_ROUND_DIR/merged.ndjson; tp <phase> <spec> --record $TP_ROUND_DIR/merged.ndjson' for review-record and audit-record, with an unknown kind returning "" the way DurableWrite returns false; verified by a table pinning all eight strings byte for byte against the spec text, and by running each record brief through /bin/sh with a fake tp on PATH — the merge step is invoked when merged.ndjson is absent and skipped when it is present, so a re-run never merges over the dispositions §6.3 accumulates (test 57).
- UnitKind.Succeeded(exitCode, target) is the driver's whole success test — exit 0 AND the kind's durable write present — verified over the four combinations: only exit 0 with the write present succeeds, and both an exit 0 with nothing written and a non-zero exit over a complete write are failed attempts (test 51).
- Gate green before closing: go test -race ./... = 0, golangci-lint run = 0 issues, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh = 0.

tasks.title: Export the child environment variables
tasks.acceptance:
Every child receives TP_RUN_ID as a ULID, TP_RUN_DIR absolute, TP_ROUND_DIR derived from phase and round, TP_FILE, TP_UNIT_ID, TP_UNIT_KIND, TP_UNIT_SEQ and TP_PHASE.
TP_ROUND and TP_ROUND_DIR are unset, not empty, outside a round-based phase, and driver variables are applied after the runner.env merge (tests 20, 37, 46).
source_sections: #### 3.1.1 Units, ids and the child environment
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/engine/childenv.go builds every child's environment from §3.1.1: ChildEnv merges runner.env over the parent and then applies the driver's own variables last (TP_RUN_ID, TP_RUN_DIR, TP_FILE, TP_UNIT_ID, TP_UNIT_KIND, TP_UNIT_SEQ, TP_PHASE, TP_ROUND, TP_ROUND_DIR and §5.1's TP_UNATTENDED=1); NewULID emits the canonical 26-character Crockford ULID for TP_RUN_ID, RunDir resolves the absolute .tp/runs/<run-id>, RunBase strips the .tasks.json suffix for the run artifacts' <base>, and RoundDir derives .tp/rounds/<base>/<phase>-r<round>. Verified by tests asserting every variable's documented form, TP_RUN_DIR absolute, the round directory keyed by base+phase+round, and the ULID's alphabet, length, uniqueness over 200 draws and decoded timestamp.
- TP_ROUND and TP_ROUND_DIR are removed rather than emptied when the oracle reports round null, even when the parent environment or runner.env carried them (test 46), and driver variables outrank runner.env so an entry for TP_UNATTENDED, TP_RUN_ID, TP_ROUND_DIR or TP_UNIT_KIND never reaches the child while non-driver entries still extend and override the parent (test 20). Gate green: go test -race ./... 0, golangci-lint run 0, scripts/check-deadcode.sh 0.
Out of scope: nothing found.

tasks.title: Take a run-scoped lock
tasks.acceptance:
tp run takes .tp/locks/run-<base>.lock for the whole run and never holds the task-file write lock while a child is in flight.
A child's own tp write succeeds during the run and a second tp run exits 4 (test 9).
source_sections: #### 3.1.1 Units, ids and the child environment
tasks.closed_reason:
- engine.WithRunLock takes the run-scoped lock $3.1.1 fixes — .tp/locks/run-<base>.lock, from RunLockPath, a distinct file from LockFilePath's task-file write lock — for the whole callback, and refuses a second acquirer with *RunLockBusyError on a single TryLock rather than the write lock's retry-with-backoff, because a run's holder is a whole run and no timeout outlasts it; internal/cli/root.go maps that error to exit 4 (STATE) beside the existing LockTimeoutError branch, so tp run inherits the exit code the moment driver-loop lands.
- The driver never holds the task-file write lock while a child is in flight: a real child process's tp set lands in under a second while this process holds the run lock (internal/cli/run_lock_test.go), and a second acquirer of the run lock is refused in the same window; engine tests pin the literal path, the prompt refusal, the reacquisition after release, the zero-byte marker surviving release (the flock-inode rule) and the .tp/.gitignore entry.
- Verified by running: both new test files were watched failing first (undefined symbols), then two mutations were applied and their blast radius read — neutering the !locked guard reddened exactly the two refusal tests, and pointing RunLockPath at LockFilePath reddened the distinctness and free-write tests plus the CLI test, whose child tp set then timed out at exit 4 after 5.03s, reproducing the deadlock the guard prevents. Gate green run separately: go test -race ./... = 0, golangci-lint run = 0, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh = 0.
Out of scope: the end-to-end "a second tp run exits 4" assertion cannot run until tp run exists (driver-loop); the dispatcher branch and RunLockBusyError.Hint() are in place and unit-covered, so that task only needs to call WithRunLock and return its error.

tasks.title: Add next_units to the resume oracle
tasks.acceptance:
tp resume --json gains next_units carrying {kind, id, brief_command} plus round, and next_action renders next_units[0].
A non-concurrent kind is never returned alongside another unit, and every assertion pinning resume's exact object set moves with the field (test 38).
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp resume --json now carries next_units — an ordered array of {kind, id, brief_command} — beside round: the round the returned units belong to (len(recorded)+1 in review and audit, null in implement/decompose/release), both built in internal/engine/nextunits.go and surfaced by internal/cli/resume.go; verified end to end by internal/cli/resume_next_units_test.go, which pins each entry's exact three keys for the implement, decompose, review-role and audit-role phases, asserts round advances after tp review --record, and checks the array survives --compact.
- next_action renders next_units[0]: renderNextAction copies the phase payload and adds unit={kind,id} naming the first entry, so the human object and the machine surface can never describe different work; asserted for every non-empty phase (and its absence for release and a blocked phase) plus a unit test that the caller's payload is not mutated.
- A non-concurrent kind is never returned alongside another unit: soloIfNotConcurrent is the single chokepoint, tested over all eight UnitKinds rather than over the phases that emit one today, including a concurrent-then-non-concurrent array. brief_command comes from UnitKind.BriefCommand so no command string is spelled twice.
- next_units is [] (never null) in §4.1's three empty cases — release, a blocked phase, and a phase held by an escalate blocker (raising a round cap, an unmet dependency chain, a stale spec) — and the role panel is resolved exactly as tp review/tp audit resolve it, so a spec's enabled:false role is not spawned; dogfooded on this repo (implement/next-units, round null) and on spec/0.36.0.md (review, round 1, the custom 4-reviewer corpus).
- The assertions pinning resume's object set moved with the field: internal/cli/resume_payload_test.go's decompose payload now expects the rendered unit, and a new TestResume_ObjectSet pins the exact top-level key set. Gate green: go test -race ./... 0, golangci-lint run 0, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh 0.
Out of scope: the record/resolve/fix kinds and the predicate-driven omission of already-satisfied roles are round-resumption's acceptance, so a round-based phase currently returns its whole role panel every time.

tasks.title: Omit roles already satisfying the predicate
tasks.acceptance:
In a round-based phase next_units omits every role whose findings file satisfies the role predicate, and a malformed file is re-run rather than skipped.
After a round is recorded the oracle returns one audit-fix unit at a time and one review-resolve unit while a finding lacks a disposition (tests 45, 52).
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/engine/nextunits.go's new roundBasedUnits filters the collecting round's role panel through the role kind's own DurableWrite over $TP_ROUND_DIR/role-<id>.ndjson — the same §3.3 predicate the driver and the Stop hook read — so a role whose file is present and wholly parseable is omitted while one that left a malformed file, or none at all, is returned; the round directory is the collecting round's own, resolved from the repo root now threaded through BuildNextUnits from AssembleResume. Verified by engine and CLI tests watched failing first (all three roles returned) and by mutating the omission into a no-op, which reddened exactly the four omission tests and nothing else.
- After a round is recorded, dispositionUnit reads that round's merged.ndjson and returns a single review-resolve unit (id: the spec base name) while any finding lacks a resolved object, or a single audit-fix unit keyed role:item_id for the first row that is neither PASS nor already disposed — one at a time, with round reporting the round just recorded rather than the next, and no unit at all when the merged file is absent or unparseable. Verified by tests watched failing first and by two further mutations (disabling the recorded-round branch; dropping the PASS/disposed filter), each reddening exactly the expected tests, plus a live dogfood of the freshly built binary through all four states (partial round, satisfied panel, undisposed merged file, fully disposed).
- The record-unit emission is deliberately left to the record-units task: a non-empty panel with nothing pending returns no unit today, and the panel and the pending roles are kept as separate values so §4.1's non-empty guard can be added there without restructuring.

tasks.title: Store last_failure outside the run state
tasks.acceptance:
A non-zero unit exit writes .tp/last_failure-<base>.json with the documented fields and a tp-authored summary, cleared only on the next success of the same (kind, id).
tp resume and tp brief surface it and it survives into the next run (test 23).
tasks.closed_reason:
- A non-zero unit exit writes .tp/last_failure-<base>.json with section 4.2's six fields (unit_kind, unit_id, phase, exit_code, summary, at) and a tp-authored summary naming the failing command and the log path, never the child's prose (internal/engine/lastfailure.go plus the driver's recordLastFailure/failureSummary); a second failure overwrites it and a success clears it only when the (unit_kind, unit_id) pair matches, since id alone collides between the two record kinds.
- tp resume carries last_failure as a top-level key that survives --compact and is null when there is none (the section 10.8 object-set assertion moved with the field), and tp brief plus tp next --brief carry it under an omitempty key with a Last failure section rendered right after Identity; it lives outside the run state, so a second run neither clears nor rewrites it (test 23).
- Verified by running: the driver and surface tests were written first and watched fail against unchanged code (no file written; last_failure key absent), then four mutations were confirmed to redden exactly the right tests and restored byte-identically — dropping the kind from the clear key reddened only the clear-key test, writing on !succeeded() instead of a non-zero exit reddened only the exit-0-no-durable-write test, neutering the clear branch reddened only the clear test, and nil-ing both reads reddened the three surfacing tests while leaving the null-without-record test green. Gate green separately: go test -race ./... 0, golangci-lint run 0, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh 0; dogfooded with a freshly built binary on a scratch project across tp resume (JSON and TTY), tp brief and tp next --brief, present and absent.
Out of scope: .tp/.gitignore still does not list .tp/run-<base>.json, .tp/runs/, .tp/rounds/ or .tp/last_failure-<base>.json — that is the gitignore-entries task (test 15).

tasks.title: Record a gate failure from tp done
tasks.acceptance:
tp done writes last_failure with the gate's own output when its gate fails and TP_UNIT_KIND is set.
It writes nothing when that variable is absent, leaving the shipped command unchanged outside a run (test 61).
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp done now writes section 4.2's last_failure when the quality gate it ran fails and TP_UNIT_KIND is set: internal/cli/gate.go's recordGateFailure takes unit_kind, unit_id and phase from the child environment, exit_code from the gate itself, and a tp-authored summary naming the gate command and carrying the gate's own output tail (falling back to the failure message when the gate said nothing), never the closing agent's prose; both entry points are covered, the pre-flock path used by tp done and tp done <ids>, and the batch path, which does not exit through runQualityGatePreFlock and so records the failure itself.
- Outside a run it writes nothing at all: TP_UNIT_KIND is the fence, since the record's unit_kind, unit_id and phase have no value there, and the shipped error object (gate_cmd, exit_code, output_tail, hint) and exit 4 are unchanged. tp close passes the new recordFailure parameter as false, so the writer stays the one the spec names.
- Verified by running: all eight tests in internal/cli/last_failure_gate_test.go were written first and watched fail against the unchanged binary, then four mutations each reddened exactly the right tests - dropping the TP_UNIT_KIND fence reddened only the outside-a-run test, removing the pre-flock record call reddened the four pre-flock positives while the batch test stayed green, forcing the recorded exit code to 4 reddened the four exit-code assertions, and ignoring recordFailure reddened only the tp close test; each was restored byte-identically (gate.go sha256 aca9e8d7...). A fifth mutation, emptying the summary's output, first survived because the assertion searched for a token the gate command also contained - the gate was changed to print a string absent from its own command text, after which the mutation reddened the two output-carrying tests.
- Dogfooded with the freshly built binary on a scratch project: the same failing gate leaves no file outside a run and writes .tp/last_failure-spec.json under TP_UNIT_KIND, and tp next --brief then surfaces that record.
- Gate green, each step run separately: go test -race ./... 0, golangci-lint run 0, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh 0.
- Out of scope: nothing found.

tasks.title: Write the run state file
tasks.acceptance:
.tp/run-<base>.json holds run_id, started_at, phase, stop_reason, totals and one row per unit attempt, written atomically.
A row is appended with null exit_code before its child spawns and updated after it exits, and totals restart at zero on a new run (test 12).
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/engine/runstate.go writes §3.5's run state at .tp/run-<base>.json (RunStatePath, named per task file off RunBase and absolute like TP_RUN_DIR): RunState carries run_id, started_at, phase, stop_reason, totals {units, wall_clock_seconds, spend_usd} and one RunUnitRow per unit attempt {seq, kind, id, attempt, exit_code, duration_seconds, spend_usd, log_path}; every mutation rewrites the whole file through a unique temp file + rename, serialized by the recorder's mutex because concurrent role siblings finish in the same iteration and readers take no lock. Verified by tests asserting the documented top-level shape and the path form, and by eight concurrent siblings under -race with a lock-free reader beside them: every row survives, the file always parses and no .tmp is left behind.
- RunRecorder.StartUnit appends the row before the child is spawned with exit_code, duration_seconds and spend_usd forced to null (cleared from a copy, so the caller's value is untouched), and FinishUnit updates that row in place by seq — a seq no row carries is an error rather than an invented row. Totals are recomputed from the rows on every write, so units counts attempts (a retry is a second row) and spend sums only the metered ones, an unmetered unit staying null and accruing nothing. NewRunRecorder replaces any file a dead run left at the path, so units, spend, wall clock and stop_reason all restart at zero on a new run — caps bound a run, not a cycle. Verified by test 12's before/after assertions read from the raw JSON (null vs 0 is the distinction the two-write protocol rests on), an attempts test that agrees with Snapshot's accrual, and a second-run test asserting zeroed totals, no inherited rows and a fresh run_id.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... (0), golangci-lint run (0 issues), ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh (0).
Out of scope: the run state is not yet reachable from any command — ReadRunState and Snapshot exist for the run-status and cap tasks that own those surfaces, and the .tp/.gitignore entry for run-<base>.json belongs to gitignore-entries.

tasks.title: Own each unit's log file
tasks.acceptance:
A template omitting {log_path} has its child's stdout and stderr redirected to $TP_RUN_DIR/<seq>-<kind>-<id>.jsonl; one using the placeholder owns the file and is not redirected.
Every child is spawned with stdin closed so a runner reading stdin sees EOF (tests 60, 62).
tasks.closed_reason:
- The driver now owns the log of a template that omits {log_path} (section 3.5): unitAttempt.spawn opens $TP_RUN_DIR/<seq>-<kind>-<id>.jsonl and points both stdout and stderr at that one descriptor, while a runner whose resolved argv already carries the path owns the file and is not redirected; a log the driver cannot open is a driver error rather than a failed attempt. Verified by writing the pair first and watching the redirect arm fail for the right reason (no such file) against unchanged code, then by two mutations: forcing the redirect unconditional reddened only the owns-the-file arm on the log existing, and dropping cmd.Stderr reddened only the redirect arm on the missing to-stderr line. Restore checksum-verified byte-identical.
- Every child is spawned with stdin closed, so a runner reading stdin sees EOF (test 62): both arms drive a script runner that reads stdin to completion and writes a marker afterwards, asserting the marker exists (the read returned rather than blocking) and the capture is empty. This pins existing behaviour rather than proving new code — cmd.Stdin = nil is Go's own default — so the discriminating evidence is the mutation: handing the child a strings.Reader reddened the stdin assertion in both arms while every log assertion stayed green.
- Out of scope: the owns-the-file arm's argv assertion and the run-state log-path assertion also passed before the change; they are pinned contract, and only the file-absence assertion in that arm discriminates against an over-redirecting driver.

tasks.title: Execute the driver loop
tasks.acceptance:
tp run [spec] reads cycle state, takes next_units, spawns concurrent kinds together and every other kind alone, re-reads state from disk, and checks caps.
The loop advances through implement, review and audit and stops with converged when the oracle reports phase release; a crashed driver resumes at the same unit (tests 2, 5, 6).
tasks.closed_reason:
- engine.RunDriver in internal/engine/driver.go is section 3.1 as written: each iteration reads the cycle through AssembleResume (the same path tp resume uses, re-reading the task file from disk every time), stops converged when the oracle reports phase release, stops no-units on an empty next_units, spawns one runner process per unit through ResolveUnitRunner with concurrent kinds together and every other kind alone (concurrentBatch), and checks the unit, wall-clock and budget caps between iterations in section 3.4 precedence order; internal/cli/run.go adds tp run, resolving its cycle through the resolveCycle extracted from tp resume and holding the run-scoped lock for the whole run.
- The loop advances phases and stops converged, proven by running rather than reading: two implement units taken in sequence to a release stop, the review and audit role panels fanned out and their overlap asserted from the children own clocks, each role .part renamed to the final name by the driver (section 3.3.1), a role leftover cleared before the attempt (section 3.1.1), and a crashed driver resuming at the same unit across two runs. Every loop test is bounded so a loop that never answers fails rather than hangs. All ten tests were watched failing against an inert stub first, then eight mutations were applied and reverted byte-identically (verified by checksum): concurrentBatch pass-through reddened only its two non-concurrent cases, the .part rename no-op only the role-concurrency test, the leftover clearing no-op only the leftover test, capStop always-empty only the cap test, allSucceeded always-true only the crash-resume and leftover tests, the release check only the two converged tests, sequential spawning only the role-concurrency test, and the no-units reason swap only its own test plus the role-concurrency stop.
- Gate green and run separately: go test -race ./... 0, golangci-lint run 0, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh 0. tp run was dogfooded through the freshly built binary on a scratch project with an operator shell script as TP_RUNNER_SEAM, producing the documented payload and a run state file with one row per attempt. The command-surface baseline in nongoals_surface_test.go was rebased onto v0.34.2 and admits tp run, in the same commit that registers it, as that guard own contract requires.
- Out of scope, left as small additions for their own open tasks: retry budgets and the second attempt (retry-attempts), the remaining three stop reasons and their precedence table (stop-reasons, stop-precedence, cap-timing), converting a driver-side spawn failure into a driver-error stop rather than a returned error (driver-error), the exit-code mapping so a non-converged stop exits 4 (run-exit-codes), reading spend from the runner final log line so spend_usd stays null and cap-budget inert (runner-spend), the stdout/stderr redirect into the log path the driver already computes (unit-logs), and --status and --dry-run (run-status, run-dry-run). The loop cannot yet cross out of a collected review or audit round because the oracle does not emit the round record unit (record-units); the review and audit tests assert the honest no-units stop that follows, and will assert the crossing when that task lands.

tasks.title: Attempt a unit its budgeted number of times
tasks.acceptance:
A unit is attempted 1 + run_max_unit_retries times, each attempt taking a fresh seq and log path.
The driver deletes a role unit's findings file and any stale .part immediately before spawning it, so a leftover cannot satisfy the retry's predicate (tests 8, 17, 65).
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/engine/driver.go now attempts a unit 1 + run_max_unit_retries times (section 3.4): attemptBudget reads the resolved workflow field, runIteration re-spawns only the units whose attempt failed, and each retry goes back through prepare so it takes a fresh seq, a fresh log path and a run-state row carrying its own attempt number; exhausting the budget stops the run with unit-failure, and a driver-side spawn failure still returns as an error rather than being charged as a failed attempt.
- Verified by running, never by reading: the three new driver tests were watched failing first (1 attempt where 2 and 3 were expected, unit-failure where converged was expected, a stale .part still present), and the count is pinned exactly at retries 0, 1 and 2 rather than as 'more than one attempt'. Mutating attemptBudget into a no-op reddened exactly the four retry tests; pinning Attempt to 1 reddened only the attempt-counter assertion; disabling the role-artifact clear reddened the new retry test and the existing first-attempt one. driver.go was restored byte-identically after each mutation (sha256 checked).
- The role findings file and any stale .part are deleted immediately before every attempt, not only the first (section 3.1.1): the fake runner's TP_FAKE_RUNNER_DURABLE knob is now a per-invocation list so an attempt that writes nothing can follow one that wrote a .part, which is the only arrangement in which a driver that fails to clear behaves differently from one that clears.
- Gate green, each step run separately: go test -race ./... = 0, golangci-lint run = 0, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh = 0.
Out of scope: tp next claimed run-status before this unit was redirected to retry-attempts, so run-status is left wip; tp reopen refuses a wip task (done only), so it needs the next unit's tp next to resume it.

tasks.title: Record the nine stop reasons
tasks.acceptance:
Each of the nine stop_reason values is produced by its documented cause, and run_max_units, totals.units and units-done all count attempts.
No stop reason records a round, marks a phase converged, or closes a task its own unit did not close (tests 3, 4, 7, 33).
tasks.closed_reason:
- engine.StopReason (internal/engine/stopreason.go) is section 3.4's nine reasons as one closed, named vocabulary in the spec's cause-table order — converged, cap-units, cap-wall-clock, cap-budget, escalation, unit-failure, no-units, interrupted, driver-error — replacing the six untyped string constants the loop carried and naming the three (escalation, interrupted, driver-error) that had no name at all; RunRecorder.Stop is the one writer of stop_reason and now refuses anything outside the nine at that sink, so a reason no reader can match on is never recorded. Every reason the loop's own causes reach is produced by that cause and by no other: converged at phase release, no-units on an empty next_units, unit-failure on an attempt that did not succeed, and each cap from its own counter — proved by driving real runs through TP_RUNNER_SEAM plus a capStop table whose negative rows hold the other two counters far from their caps. run_max_units and totals.units are one counter, the recorder's rows, one per attempt: a three-role panel reads 3 in the driver's result, in totals.units and in the row count, and two rows for the same unit count twice, so units-done cannot disagree with either.
- The negative invariant was driven, not read: a cap stop in a collecting review round leaves zero review and zero audit rounds recorded and the phase at review rather than release, and a cap stop in the implement phase with a converged audit behind it leaves the second task open, the audit rounds at the two it found, and only the task its own unit closed done.
- Watched red first: the whole test file failed to compile against the unnamed constants. Then four mutations, each restored byte-identically and checksum-verified — cap-units reading the wall-clock counter reddened the units rows and left the wall-clock row green; the wall-clock arm returning StopCapUnits (right cause, wrong reason) reddened exactly the two wall-clock assertions and nothing else; dropping the Known guard reddened only the recorder refusal; counting distinct units instead of rows reddened only the attempt counters. Gate run separately: go test -race 0, golangci-lint 0, check-deadcode 0.
- Out of scope: escalation, interrupted and driver-error are named here but not yet produced — their causes are the open escalation-detection, cap-timing and driver-error tasks, which this leaves untouched; likewise retry-attempts owns the retry loop (the counter it feeds is pinned here), stop-precedence the ordering among simultaneously satisfied reasons, run-exit-codes the 0-on-converged/4-otherwise mapping, and run-status the units-done rendering of totals.units. cap-budget is covered over the recorder's real accrual rather than end to end because the driver still passes nil spend until the open runner-spend task reads the runner's final log line.

tasks.title: Order simultaneously satisfied stop reasons
tasks.acceptance:
When one checkpoint satisfies several rows the recorded reason is the documented first, with converged leading.
Two simultaneously satisfied conditions record the higher-precedence reason (test 34).
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/engine/stopreason.go now carries section 3.4's precedence order as data: stopPrecedence lists the nine in the documented order (converged, driver-error, escalation, unit-failure, interrupted, cap-budget, cap-wall-clock, cap-units, no-units), with stopRank and highestPrecedence over it, so a checkpoint hands in every condition it found true and the order alone decides which is recorded. Verified by a test that recovers the vocabulary from the package's own StopReason declarations with go/ast and fails until a tenth reason is placed, and by asserting the earlier of every pair the order can form wins from either argument order.
- internal/engine/driver.go's loop now judges releasability, the operator's signal, the three caps, an empty next_units and what the previous iteration left at that one ranked checkpoint, carrying the iteration's outcome into the next read instead of answering it where it was produced. The caps were checked at the end of the iteration body, so a run that reached one on the very iteration that released the cycle recorded the cap; that was reproduced as a failing test first, on both the unit and the wall-clock counter, and section 5.2's escalation case (converged still leads an escalation raised in the same iteration) reproduced the same way. Each pair is driven twice, once with both conditions true and once as a control that trips only the loser and records it, and the losing condition is asserted from what the run left behind (capStop over the recorded totals, the escalation record on disk, DryRunUnits reporting nothing pending), so a run that tripped one condition alone cannot pass for the wrong reason. unit-failure over cap-units and cap-units over no-units are pinned the same way.
- Mutation checks, each restored byte-identically: collapsing stopRank to a constant reddened both converged-over-cap arms, converged-over-escalation, the ordering tests and every other converged assertion, and nothing else; reinstating the old immediate escalation return reddened exactly the converged-over-escalation arm; disabling the interrupted-mid-retry branch reddened exactly the signal-spends-no-retry test. The first mutation was informative twice over: it showed that collecting the conditions in precedence order would let a broken rank go on producing right answers, so checkpoint now collects them in an order deliberately unlike it, converged last of all.
- Quality gate run separately: go test -race ./... exit 0, golangci-lint run exit 0 with 0 issues, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh exit 0.

tasks.title: Evaluate caps between iterations only
tasks.acceptance:
Caps are checked between iterations, in-flight children run to completion and the driver kills nothing.
SIGINT and SIGTERM stop the run with interrupted, letting children finish and spawning no new unit (tests 41, 63).
tasks.closed_reason:
- Caps stay evaluated between iterations only and the driver kills nothing (test 63): driven as a real run whose three role children sleep 1500ms past a one-second wall-clock cap, then asserted as an absence — every claimed fake-runner record slot also holds a completed record, every run-state row carries an exit code, and each child exited after started_at plus the cap, so the deadline passed with the panel still alive. Mutating spawn into exec.CommandContext with a 1.3s timeout (a driver that kills) turned that equality into 0 completed against 3 claimed; the restore was checksum-verified.
- SIGINT and SIGTERM now stop the run with interrupted (test 41): internal/engine/interrupt.go watches both for the run's duration and the loop reads the watch before spawning, before a retry and before the caps, so a signalled run lets its in-flight children finish, spawns no new unit and writes stop_reason before exiting. Both signals were delivered for real to the driver process mid-panel — the tests failed first with no-units and unit-failure, and a retry test went from 2 attempts to 1 — and mutating signalled() into a never-observe no-op reddened exactly those three tests and nothing else. Dogfooded on a scratch project: a real tp run SIGINT left its sleep-30 child running to completion, exited 4 and recorded interrupted in .tp/run-spec.json.
- Out of scope: capStop still runs at the end of the iteration body, before the next readCycle, so a run reaching a cap on the iteration that made the cycle releasable records the cap rather than converged, which section 3.4's converged-leads rule forbids — that is a precedence change rather than this task's timing fence. Separately, children share the driver's process group, so a terminal Ctrl-C reaches them directly; making in-flight children finish under that delivery too would need Setpgid, which no section of the spec asks for.

tasks.title: Stop on a driver-side fatal error
tasks.acceptance:
A runner that cannot be exec'd, or a run directory that cannot be written, stops the run with driver-error and exit 4.
No unit is charged a failed attempt for it (test 70).
tasks.closed_reason:
- A driver-side fatal error (section 3.4) now stops the run with driver-error and exits 4: engine.DriverError names the class, RunDriver's fail() records StopDriverError for it and only for it, and internal/cli/root.go's dispatchError maps it to ExitState (4) with its own hint, after the two runner-shape branches that keep exit 2. Verified by driving a real exec failure through TP_RUNNER_SEAM pointed at a nonexistent path (test 70 arm 1) and a run directory placed under a regular file (arm 2), watching both fail first against unchanged code, and dogfooded with the freshly built binary on a scratch project: exit 4, stop_reason driver-error, and tp run --status reporting run_state stopped instead of crashed.
- No unit is charged a failed attempt for it: the exec failure returns before failedUnits is consulted, proved by setting run_max_unit_retries to 2 and asserting the run state carries exactly one attempt row rather than three.
- Fixed a real bug the previous unit reported out of scope: record() called FinishUnit with exit code 0 for an attempt whose runner never exec'd, so the row read exit_code 0 for a child that does not exist. Reproduced first (the assertion saw a non-nil *int), then fixed by leaving the row's nulls, which section 3.5 already defines as never finished.
- Gate green, each step run separately: go test -race ./... = 0, golangci-lint run = 0, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh = 0. Mutation-checked all three additions: emptying fail() reddened only TestRunDriver_ARunnerThatCannotExecStopsWithDriverError, dropping record()'s continue reddened only that same test's exit_code assertion, and disabling the dispatchError branch reddened only TestDispatchError_DriverErrorIsState; every restore was checksum-verified byte-identical.
Out of scope: the full stop-reason to exit-code mapping is still absent, so tp run exits 0 on converged, cap-*, escalation, unit-failure, no-units and interrupted alike — that is the open run-exit-codes task, and this unit pinned only driver-error's 4.

tasks.title: Pin tp run's exit codes
tasks.acceptance: tp run exits 0 on converged and 4 on every other stop_reason, and 2 on a usage error before the loop starts (test 54).
tasks.closed_reason:
- runExitCode in internal/cli/run.go is section 3.4's exit-code sentence: tp run exits 0 on converged and 4 on every other stop_reason, decided after the payload is written so a caller reading stdout and one branching on the exit code are told the same thing about the same run; it is a whitelist of the one converging reason, so an unmapped or empty reason exits 4 rather than being accepted as convergence.
- Exhaustiveness is derived rather than remembered: run_exit_codes_internal_test.go parses every StopReason constant out of the engine package's own sources (the engine exports no enumerator over the nine — Known() answers membership one value at a time and cannot be walked) and requires the contract table to cover exactly them, so a tenth reason fails the package until someone maps it; verified by adding a tenth constant and watching 'tenth-reason has no exit code' before reverting it.
- Test 54 is driven through the real binary in run_exit_codes_test.go: converged exits 0 having spawned nothing, no-units, unit-failure, cap-units and escalation each exit 4 with the recorded stop reason asserted beside the code, and both usage errors (too many arguments, unknown flag) exit 2 having spawned no child, written no .tp/run-spec.json and created no .tp/runs.
- Three mutations were watched failing: returning ExitState unconditionally reddened only the converged arm; returning ExitSuccess unconditionally reddened all eight non-converged table rows and the four end-to-end exit-4 runs; and mapping an unknown reason to 0 — right for the eight it names, wrong by rule — reddened only TestRunExitCode_AnUnnamedReasonIsNotConvergence, so the whitelist direction is the assertion that discriminates it. run.go was then restored byte-identically.
- Four pre-existing tp run --status fixtures and the driver test drove non-converged runs while asserting exit 0 and were updated to 4. Gate green run separately: go test -race ./... 0, golangci-lint run 0, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh 0. Dogfooded on a scratch project with TP_RUNNER_SEAM plus internal/fakerunner: a real unit-failure run printed its payload and exited 4, .tp/runs was created, and both usage errors exited 2.

tasks.title: Report the run with tp run --status
tasks.acceptance:
tp run --status prints phase, units done, spend against each cap, the last unit's exit code and log path, stop_reason, and run_state as in_flight, crashed or stopped using the run lock.
It carries the divergence signals on an audit-phase stop, exits 0 when it can report and 3 when no run state exists, and takes no lock (tests 14, 35, 58).
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp run --status reports the current or last run from .tp/run-<base>.json (internal/cli/run_status.go, wired as a --status flag on tp run): phase, run_id, started_at, units_done, wall_clock_seconds and spend_usd beside a caps object carrying run_max_units, run_max_wall_clock_seconds and run_max_budget_usd, the last unit's whole row (exit code and log path included), and stop_reason; verified end to end against a real run through TP_RUNNER_SEAM and dogfooded on a scratch project with the freshly built binary.
- run_state is stopped once stop_reason is set, otherwise in_flight when the run lock is held and crashed when it is not, using the new engine.RunLockHeld probe (TryLock plus immediate Unlock; a missing lock file reads as not held and none is created); verified by one test that runs all three arms over one hand-written run state in one directory, the last arm re-reading with the lock FILE present but unheld, and by mutating the probe to always report unheld, which reddened only the in_flight assertion.
- The report exits 0 whenever it can report and 3 when no run state exists for the resolved task file, and takes no run lock — the in_flight arm above reports while a lock is held; the exit-3 path has its own fixture (a cycle never driven), watched failing first and re-verified by mutating the branch to exit 4, which reddened only that test.
- units_done counts attempts rather than distinct units, matching totals.units and what run_max_units bounds (section 3.4); proved with a run whose one unit was attempted twice, and by mutating units_done to count distinct (kind,id) pairs, which reddened only that test while the four-distinct-unit fixture stayed green.
- On an audit-phase stop the payload also carries role_streaks, spec_coverage_clean_rounds and divergence, computed from the same inputs as tp audit --status and asserted equal to that command's own output in the same fixture; both mutation arms discriminate — suppressing the block reddened only the audit-phase test, and always emitting reddened only the non-audit-phase absence assertions.
- Gate green, each step run separately: go test -race ./... 0, golangci-lint run 0 issues, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh 0. skills/tp/SKILL.md's inventory and the v0.34.2 surface baseline were updated in the same commit that registers the flag, as their guard tests require.
Out of scope: when a runner fails to exec, engine/driver.go's record() still calls FinishUnit with exit code 0, so the run state row for a unit that never spawned reports exit_code 0 rather than staying null — section 3.5 says a row is updated when its child exits, and that child never did. Seen while dogfooding; belongs to the driver, not to this reporting command.

tasks.title: List the next units with --dry-run
tasks.acceptance: tp run --dry-run prints the units the driver would execute next, exits 0, spawns nothing, writes no run state and takes no lock (tests 13, 58).
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp run --dry-run lists the units the driver would execute next as {phase, round, next_units} and exits 0: engine.DryRunUnits reaches them through the driver's own first steps (the same readCycle every iteration opens with, then the same concurrentBatch that picks one iteration's batch), so the listing is the driver's answer rather than a second derivation; verified by a test asserting the implement unit and its brief_command, and by one comparing the whole array, phase and round against tp resume's own next_units in a multi-unit audit panel, so the listing is driven off the oracle's set rather than a hand-copied list.
- It spawns nothing, writes no run state and takes no run lock (tests 13 and 58): every negative half is driven through the real path, not asserted about a path not taken - the runner seam is pinned to the fake runner with a live record directory and no record appears, the task stays open, .tp/run-spec.json and .tp/runs are absent afterwards, and a dry run exits 0 while another holder owns the run lock in the same fixture whose control arm is a real tp run refused with exit 4. Mutations: routing the flag to the driving path reddened exactly the three dry-run tests, wrapping the handler in WithRunLock reddened only the lock test, and creating a run recorder reddened only the run-state assertion; the restore is byte-identical by checksum.
- Surface bookkeeping moved with the flag: the v0.34.2 command-surface baseline now reads 'run: dry-run status' and SKILL.md's flag inventory carries the sub-mode. Gate green: go test -race ./... 0, golangci-lint 0, check-deadcode.sh 0. Dogfooded on tp's own repo (empty listing, matching tp resume under the standing escalate blocker) and on a scratch project in both the implement and the three-role audit phase.

tasks.title: Strip the run surface under --compact
tasks.acceptance: Under --compact the run surface keeps stop_reason and the cap totals and strips per-unit rows and log paths (test 68).
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp run --status now omits last_unit under --compact (internal/cli/run_status.go): stop_reason, units_done, wall_clock_seconds, spend_usd and the whole caps object survive, and the per-unit row — the only carrier of log_path in the payload — is stripped, which is section 7's requirement and test 68.
- Verified by running, not reading: internal/cli/run_status_test.go TestRunStatus_CompactStripsUnitRowsAndLogPaths drives one real run through the seam, then reads it twice. The control arm requires the non-compact payload to actually carry a row with a non-empty log_path, so the strip assertions cannot pass on an empty fixture. The test was watched failing on unchanged code with exactly the two expected assertions red.
- Two mutations confirmed the discrimination: forcing the branch always-off (the right answer for the wrong reason — always strip) reddened only the control arm and TestRunStatus_ReportsAStoppedRun; forcing it always-on reddened only the two strip assertions. The file was then restored byte-identically (sha256 5c6ce7dd… before and after).
- tp run's own driving payload was checked in the same test to carry no log_path under --compact: it reports a unit COUNT, so it has no row to strip. tp run --help now states the compact behaviour.
- Gate green, each step run separately: go test -race ./... = 0, golangci-lint run = 0, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh = 0. Dogfooded on a scratch project with the freshly built binary: the full report carries last_unit with its log path, --compact carries neither and keeps caps, stop_reason and the three totals.
Out of scope: section 3.5 also specifies tp run --dry-run (print the units the driver would execute next, exit 0, no run state written); no flag registers it and no task in this cycle names it.

tasks.title: Git-ignore the run artifacts
tasks.acceptance: The shipped .tp/.gitignore covers .tp/run-<base>.json, .tp/runs/, .tp/rounds/ and .tp/last_failure-<base>.json, and the fixture gains four entries (test 15).
tasks.closed_reason:
- EnsureTPGitignore now writes six entries instead of two: section 3.5's four run artifacts (run-*.json, runs/, rounds/, last_failure-*.json) join local.json and locks/, so the run state, the per-run log directory, the per-cycle round directory and the last-failure record are git-ignored wherever tp creates or upgrades a .tp/.gitignore; the repo's own shipped .tp/.gitignore carries the same six lines.
- Verified by asking git rather than by matching strings: a new engine test initialises a throwaway repository, calls EnsureTPGitignore and runs git check-ignore over a real path of each of the four kinds, plus the negative half that .tp/config.json, the role corpus and .tp/.gitignore itself stay committable. A second test reads the repo's own committed file. Both were written first and watched failing against unchanged code.
- Mutation-checked twice with byte-identical restores (sha256 confirmed): replacing run-*.json with *.json kept every positive assertion green and reddened only the three committable-path assertions, and replacing the two globs with the spec's literal run-<base>.json / last_failure-<base>.json placeholders reddened exactly those two ignore assertions while the others stayed green - so both the too-broad and the present-but-never-matching failure modes are discriminated.
- Test 15's fixture updates land in the same commits as the field they pin: both exact-content assertions in projectconfig_test.go gained the four entries, and the concurrency preserve fixture gained them too; reverting that fixture alone reddens the preserve test with real lost user entries, which is the defect it guards.
- Gate green, each step run separately: go test -race ./... = 0, golangci-lint run = 0, ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh = 0. Dogfooded the freshly built binary on a scratch git project: tp init wrote the six lines, and git status -uall showed none of the four artifact kinds while .tp/config.json, .tp/.gitignore, the spec and the task file stayed visible.
- Out of scope: skills/tp/REFERENCE.md and SKILL.md stated that .tp/.gitignore covers only local.json and locks/ and is rewritten when one of 'the two required lines' is missing, which this change falsified, so those three sentences were corrected in place; the wider docs-surface gaps (REFERENCE's workflow-field table and SKILL's TP_UNATTENDED section) were left to the docs-surface task.

tasks.title: Refuse user-only decisions when unattended
tasks.acceptance:
Under TP_UNATTENDED each of the four user-only operations exits 2 with its hint and exits 0 without the variable; a cap set to an equal or lower non-zero value exits 0, and a budget field set to 0 while a non-zero value resolves exits 2.
The env layer is ignored for every fenced field, runner and notify_cmd cannot be set at any layer, and the mode activates on any present non-empty value other than 0 (tests 19, 40, 64).
tasks.closed_reason:
- All four of section 5.1's user-only operations now exit 2 under TP_UNATTENDED with a hint naming them a user-approved decision and pointing at tp escalate: tp done --skip-gate (and the same decision at its other sinks, a batch entry's skip_gate and tp close --skip-gate), tp import --force, and a tp set --workflow raise of review_max_rounds/audit_max_rounds or of any run_max_* cap; each exits 0 without the variable. Every test was written first and watched failing against unchanged code.
- The comparison is against the currently resolved value, so an equal or lower non-zero value exits 0, while 0 exits 2 wherever a non-zero value resolves for a field whose 0 means disabled (both round budgets and both run budgets) and is accepted where 0 already resolves; run_max_unit_retries=0 stays the strictest value and is accepted.
- The env layer is ignored for every fenced field: the fence reads only the resolved on-disk layers, proved by a test where TP_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS=50 leaves 40 a refused raise against the resolved 5. Mutating the fence to consult TP_<FIELD> reddened exactly that test and no other.
- runner and notify_cmd are refused at every layer tp can write (tp set --workflow, --workflow --project and --local), and the mode activates on any present non-empty value other than 0. Mutating UnattendedActive to value == "1" reddened only the two activation-vocabulary tests; dropping the zero-means-disabled branch reddened only the 0-semantics assertions.
- Making the acceptance testable required the five run_max_* fields to become settable through tp set --workflow and its --project form, which they were not: this adds decimal parsing and range checks for the two budget fields and write paths for all five. No other task owned that surface.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... 0, golangci-lint run 0, scripts/check-deadcode.sh 0. The freshly built binary was dogfooded on a scratch project for every refusal and every accepted write.
Out of scope: no environment layer exists in the workflow resolver today, so the 'env layer is ignored' property is structural rather than a live layer being suppressed; the mutation above is what makes the test discriminating. skills/tp/REFERENCE.md's workflow field table still omits the seven run fields and SKILL.md carries no TP_UNATTENDED section, both owned by docs-surface.

tasks.title: Add the tp escalate command
tasks.acceptance:
tp escalate writes $TP_RUN_DIR/$TP_UNIT_SEQ-escalation.json with the documented fields and one of the five decision values, and exits 2.
Two concurrent siblings each write their own, and outside a run it is a usage error (test 22).
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp escalate writes $TP_RUN_DIR/$TP_UNIT_SEQ-escalation.json with section 5.2's seven fields (decision, unit_kind, unit_id, phase, evidence, options[], at) and exits 2; the identity fields come from the child environment tp run exports, at is stamped by tp in RFC3339Nano, and options is [] rather than null. Verified by writing every test first and watching each fail against unchanged code (unknown command "escalate"), then dogfooding the freshly built binary on a scratch run directory.
- The decision is closed over the five documented values (skip-gate, raise-review-cap, raise-audit-cap, import-force, other); a near-miss such as skipgate, skip_gate or SKIP-GATE is a usage error that writes no record, and blank or missing evidence is refused the same way.
- Two concurrent siblings sharing one TP_RUN_DIR each write their own record, since the path is keyed by TP_UNIT_SEQ rather than by unit id; a test runs both processes concurrently and reads both records back.
- Outside a run (TP_RUN_DIR unset) it is a usage error naming the missing variable and writing nothing anywhere (test 22).
- Mutation-checked three ways, each restored byte-identical (checksums compared): dropping the options normalization reddened only the empty-array test; removing the TP_RUN_DIR guard kept exit 2 but reddened the outside-a-run test on the wrong variable name; opening the decision set reddened exactly the four near-miss cases and left the empty-decision case green.

tasks.closed_reason:

tasks.title: Invoke notify_cmd on a non-converged stop
tasks.acceptance:
notify_cmd fires on every non-converged stop, exec'd without a shell and split on whitespace, carrying TP_STOP_REASON, TP_RUN_ID and on an escalation TP_ESCALATION_PATH.
Its own failure is reported and never changes stop_reason (test 42).
tasks.closed_reason:
- notify_cmd fires at driver.stop, the single sink every stop passes through, for every reason other than converged. engine.InvokeNotify runs it directly with strings.Fields and no shell, so a semicolon, a variable reference or a run of spaces in the configured string reaches the child as literal argument text. Verified by a table driven off the stop vocabulary itself (stopPrecedence), so a tenth reason is exercised the moment it exists, and by an argv assertion that a shell would fail.
- The environment carries TP_STOP_REASON, TP_RUN_ID and, on an escalation only, TP_ESCALATION_PATH. All three are removed from the inherited environment before the run values are appended, so a stale TP_ESCALATION_PATH cannot be read as this stop record, and its absence on every other stop is a fact rather than an empty string. Two end-to-end runs through TP_RUNNER_SEAM pin the escalation and the unit-failure arms.
- A notify_cmd that fails changes nothing: the outcome travels on DriverResult.Notify and tp run reports it under notify {cmd, exit_code, error}, while the exit code is still decided over stop_reason alone. Covered for a non-zero exit, a command that cannot be run at all, an unset command and a whitespace-only one (section 5.2, test 42).
- Every test was written first and watched failing against unchanged code. Mutations: an unconditional call reddened only the converged row; removing the call reddened all eight notify tests; dropping the escalation-path guard and dropping the stale-variable removal each reddened only the absent-path test; running the command through /bin/sh reddened the no-shell test and the exec-failure test. No mutation survived, and every file was restored byte-identically under sha256.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... 0, golangci-lint run 0, scripts/check-deadcode.sh 0. Dogfooded with the freshly built binary on a scratch project for a unit-failure stop and for a real tp escalate stop.

Out of scope: a driver-error stop invokes notify_cmd but never reports the outcome, because tp run returns the error before printing the payload, and that reporting channel belongs to section 3.4. notify_cmd is run unbounded, so a hanging notification hangs a driver whose run has otherwise ended - section 6.4 bounds hooks only. README.md and skills/tp/SKILL.md still carry no notify_cmd description (docs-surface).
